---
title: "Nested logit models and mediation/attenuation"
subtitle: "Example 6.2 of Mize, Doan, and Long (2019)"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

One of the most common cross-model questions is whether an effect changes when
controls are added, such as in tests of mediation/attenuation. Here the effect of a college degree on the probability of being very happy is compared between a bivariate logit and a logit with a full set of controls. Because the outcome is binary, the marginal effect is a discrete change in the predicted probability, and comparing it across models is not subject to the rescaling problem that makes comparing logit coefficients across models misleading.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/gss_cme", clear
drop if year < 2000
drop if employed != 1
drop if missing(vhappy, college, wages, occprest, age, married, parent, woman, conserv, reltrad)

quietly logit vhappy i.college, vce(robust)
estimates store mod1

quietly logit vhappy i.college i.married i.parent i.woman i.conserv ///
              i.reltrad i.year c.age##c.age, vce(robust)
estimates store mod2
<</dd_do>>
```

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare i.college, models(mod1 mod2)
<</dd_do>>
```

The **Difference** row tests whether the effect of college is smaller once the
controls are included. More than two nested models can be compared by running
`mecompare` for each pair of interest.
